Introduction

Park Bo Gum is a South Korean actor, singer, and musician currently signed under THE BLACK LABEL. He first gained widespread recognition for his work in television and film, and has since become one of Korea’s most prominent and well-respected entertainers. Bo Gum began his career under Blossom Entertainment, where he remained for ten years before parting ways with the agency in December 2022. The following month, in January 2023, he officially joined THE BLACK LABEL.

As a singer, Park Bo Gum made his Korean solo debut on October 12, 2018 with the release of his first digital single, “Let’s Go See the Stars.” He later expanded into the Japanese market, debuting with the single “Bloomin’” on March 20, 2019. His soft vocal style and warm image have earned him acclaim not only as an actor but also as a recording artist. Throughout his career, Bo Gum has received numerous accolades, including the Top Excellence Award at the 30th KBS Drama Awards and the Acting Award at the 16th Korea Assembly Grand Award. In 2016, he was named Gallup Korea’s Actor of the Year, becoming the youngest recipient in the award’s history.

On August 31, 2020, Park Bo Gum began his mandatory military service, enlisting in the Navy as a cultural promotion specialist, which allowed him to serve as part of the military band. He was officially discharged from duty on April 30, 2022.
